question: A 62-year-old man comes to the physician because of tremors in both hands for the past few months. He has had difficulty buttoning his shirts and holding a cup of coffee without spilling its content. He has noticed that his symptoms improve after a glass of whiskey. His maternal uncle began to develop similar symptoms around the same age. He has bronchial asthma controlled with albuterol and fluticasone. Examination shows a low-amplitude tremor bilaterally when the arms are outstretched that worsens during the finger-to-nose test. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "62-year-old man with tremors" -> "tremors improve with alcohol" -> "suggestive of essential tremor" -> "essential tremor commonly treated with beta-blockers" -> "Propranolol is a first-line treatment" -> 85%

CHAIN: "62-year-old man with bilateral tremors" -> "tremors worsen with finger-to-nose test" -> "indicates a possible movement disorder" -> "family history suggests genetic component" -> "essential tremor is likely" -> "Propranolol is effective for essential tremor" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Patient has difficulty with fine motor tasks" -> "tremors are low-amplitude and bilateral" -> "symptoms improve with alcohol" -> "indicates essential tremor" -> "Propranolol is a standard treatment" -> 88%

CHAIN: "Tremors in hands for months" -> "improvement with whiskey suggests essential tremor" -> "family history of similar symptoms" -> "essential tremor often treated with Propranolol" -> "Propranolol is appropriate pharmacotherapy" -> 92%
analysis: The patient's symptoms are consistent with essential tremor, characterized by bilateral tremors that improve with alcohol consumption. The most appropriate pharmacotherapy for essential tremor is propranolol, which is a beta-blocker that can help reduce tremor severity. Other options like primidone can also be used, but propranolol is often the first-line treatment. Levodopa is used for Parkinson's disease, which does not fit this patient's presentation. Therefore, the best choice is propranolol.
